body.translated_text: <s>Pratītyasamutpādavibhaṅgasūtra</s> (The Sūtra on the Analysis of Dependent Origination)

body.text: 0a evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ cchrāvastyāṃ viharati sma | j

children.text: tavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ
children.translated_text: -tavana, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great community of monks, twelve hundred and fifty monks.

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>J</s>-
There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks, say-

body.text: 1a pratītyasamutpādasya vo bhikṣavaḥ ādiñ ca deśayiṣyāmi vibhaṅgaṃ ca
body.translated_text: "O monks, I shall teach you the beginning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and its analysis.

children.text: ta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta bhāṣiṣye |
children.translated_text: well and thoroughly, pay attention, I shall speak.

body.translated_text: Listen to th-
What is the beginning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)?

body.text: 2b yad utāsmin satīdaṃ bhavaty asyotpādād idam utpadyate | yad utāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ | ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ sparśapratyayā vedanā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānaṃ upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ bhavapratyayā jātiḥ jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavaṃty evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati |
body.translated_text: It is thus: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is to say: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations) arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases); conditioned by <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases) arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> (becoming) arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> (birth) arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair. Thus there is the origination of this entire great mass of suffering.
This is called the beginning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).
What is the analysis?
'Conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations)' — what is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)?

children.text: t pūrvānte ajñānaṃ aparānte ajñānaṃ pūrvāntāparāṃte ajñānaṃ
children.translated_text: is: ignorance regarding the past, ignorance regarding the future, ignorance regarding both the past and the future;

body.translated_text: Th-

body.text: 4bβ adhyātmam ajñānaṃ | bahirdhā ajñānaṃ | adhyātmabahirdhā ajñānaṃ
body.translated_text: ignorance regarding the inner; ignorance regarding the outer; ignorance regarding both the inner and the outer;

body.text: 4bγ karmaṇy ajñānaṃ | vipāke ajñānaṃ karmavipāke ajñānaṃ |
body.translated_text: ignorance regarding <s>karma</s> (action); ignorance regarding <s>vipāka</s> (ripening); ignorance regarding both <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>vipāka</s> (ripening);

body.text: 4bδ buddhe ajñānaṃ | dharme ajñānaṃ saṅghe ajñānaṃ
body.translated_text: ignorance regarding the <s>Buddha</s>; ignorance regarding the <s>Dharma</s>; ignorance regarding the <s>Saṅgha</s>;

body.text: 4bε duḥkhe ajñānaṃ samudaye ajñānaṃ | nirodhe ajñānaṃ | mārge ajñānaṃ |
body.translated_text: ignorance regarding <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering); ignorance regarding <s>samudaya</s> (origination); ignorance regarding <s>nirodha</s> (cessation); ignorance regarding the <s>mārga</s> (path);
ignorance regarding causes; ignorance regarding <s>dharmas</s> arisen from causes;

children.text: vyeṣu | hīnapraṇītakṛṣṇaśuklasapratibhāgapratītyasamutpanneṣu dharmeṣv ajñānaṃ | ṣaṭsu vā punaḥ sparśāyataneṣu yathābhūtasaṃprativedhe iti |
children.translated_text: -d, inferior and superior, dark and bright, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen from dependent origination with their counterparts — ignorance; or furthermore, regarding the six <s>sparśāyatanas</s> (bases of contact), the lack of true and complete understanding.

body.translated_text: regarding wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, to be cultivated and not to be cultivat-

body.text: 4bθ yat tatra tatra yathābhūtasyājñānam adarśanam anabhisamayaḥ tamaḥ saṃmohaḥ avidyāndhakāram
body.translated_text: Whatever ignorance there is in each case — not knowing things as they truly are, not seeing, not comprehending, darkness, delusion, the blindness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) —
this is called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
'Conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (volitional formations)' — what are the <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations)?

body.text: 5b trayaḥ saṃskārāḥ kāyasaṃskārāḥ vāksaṃskārāḥ manaḥsaṃskārā iti |
body.translated_text: There are three <s>saṃskārāḥ</s> (formations): <s>kāyasaṃskāra</s> (bodily formation), <s>vāksaṃskāra</s> (verbal formation), and <s>manaḥsaṃskāra</s> (mental formation).
'Conditioned by <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations) arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)' — what is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)?

children.translated_text: consciousness, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness.

body.translated_text: The six classes of consciousness: e-
'Conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form)' — what is <s>nāma</s> (name)?

body.text: 7aβ catvāraḥ arūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ katame catvāraḥ vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ vijñānaskandhaḥ
body.translated_text: The four formless <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Which four? The <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling), the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception), the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations), and the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness).
What is <s>rūpa</s> (form)?

body.text: 7bβ yat kiñ cid rūpaṃ sarvvaṃ tac catvāri mahābhūtāni | catvāri ca mahābhūtāny upādāya
body.translated_text: Whatever <s>rūpa</s> (form) there is, all of that consists of the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) and that which is derived from the four <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements).

body.text: 7c itīdaṃ ca rūpaṃ pūrvakaṃ ca nāma tad aikadhyam abhi
body.translated_text: Thus, this <s>rūpa</s> (form) together with the aforementioned <s>nāma</s> (name), combin-
'Conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases)' — what are the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases)?

body.text: 8b ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni | cakṣur ādhyātmikam āyatanaṃ | śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jihvā kāyo mana adhyātmikam āyatanaṃ |
body.translated_text: The six internal sense-bases: the eye as an internal sense-base, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, and the mind as internal sense-bases.
'Conditioned by the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases) arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact)' — what is <s>sparśa</s> (contact)?
The six classes of contact: eye-contact, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact.
'Conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)' — what is <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)?

body.text: 10b tisro vedanāḥ sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca ||
body.translated_text: There are three <s>vedanās</s> (feelings): pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
'Conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving)' — what is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving)?

children.translated_text: <s>tṛṣṇās</s> (cravings): <s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s> (craving for sensual pleasures), <s>rūpatṛṣṇā</s> (craving for form), and <s>ārūpyatṛṣṇā</s> (craving for the formless).

body.translated_text: Thre-
'Conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)' — what is <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)?

body.text: 12b catvāry upādānāni | kāmopādānaṃ | dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ | śīlavratopādānaṃ ātmavādopādānaṃ |
body.translated_text: There are four <s>upādānas</s> (clingings): <s>kāmopādāna</s> (clinging to sensual pleasures), <s>dṛṣṭyupādāna</s> (clinging to views), <s>śīlavratopādāna</s> (clinging to rules and observances), and <s>ātmavādopādāna</s> (clinging to the doctrine of a self)."
Existence (<s>bhava</s>) is conditioned by clinging (<s>upādāna</s>). What is existence?
There are three kinds of existence: existence in the desire realm (<s>kāmabhava</s>), existence in the form realm (<s>rūpabhava</s>), and existence in the formless realm (<s>ārūpyabhava</s>).
Existence

body.text: 14b yā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ tasmiṃs tasmin satvanikāye jātiḥ saṃjātir avakrāṃtir abhinirvṛttiḥ prādurbhāvaḥ skandhapratilambho dhātupratilambhaḥ āy

children.translated_text: tion of the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the arising of the <s>skandhas</s>, the appearance of the <s>jīvitendriya</s> (life-faculty).

body.translated_text: The birth, origination, descent, manifestation, appearance of those various beings in those various classes of beings—the acquisition of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the acquisition of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the acqui-
Aging and death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) are conditioned by birth (<s>jāti</s>). What is aging (<s>jarā</s>)?

body.text: 15b yat tat khālityaṃ pālityaṃ valīpracuratā jīrṇatā | bhugnatā kubjagopānasīvaṅkatā | tilakālakācitagātratā | khurukhurupraśv

children.text: kāyatā purataḥprāgbhārakāyatā | daṇḍaviṣkaṃbhaṇatā | dhandhatvaṃ mandatvaṃ hāniḥ parihāṇi
children.translated_text: body bowed forward, reliance on a walking stick, slowness, dullness, decline, diminish-

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ paripākaḥ paribhedaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ purāṇībhāvaḥ jarjarībhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: the maturing and deterioration of the sense-faculties, the wearing out and crumbling of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (bodily constituents)—

body.translated_text: That which is balding, greying, abundance of wrinkles, decrepitude, being bent over, being stooped and bent like a rafter, a body marked with spots
this is called aging (<s>jarā</s>).
What is death (<s>maraṇa</s>)?

body.text: 16b yā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ tasmāt tasmāt satvanikāyāt* cyutiś cyavanatā bhedo 'ntarahāṇiḥ āyuṣo hāniḥ ūṣmaṇo hāniḥ jīvitendriyasya nirodhaḥ skandhānāṃ nikṣepo maraṇaṃ kālakriyā
body.translated_text: The falling away, passing, dissolution, disappearance of those various beings from those various classes of beings—the loss of lifespan, the loss of bodily warmth, the cessation of the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>), the laying down of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), death, the making of time—
this is called death (<s>maraṇa</s>).

body.text: 16d iti idaṃ ca maraṇaṃ pūrvikā ca jarā tad ubhayam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya jarāmaraṇam ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Thus, this death together with the preceding aging—these two, combined under one heading, are called aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>).
This is called the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>).

children.text: ādiñ ca deśayiṣyāmi vibhaṅgañ ca iti me yad uktam idaṃ me tat praty uktaṃ
children.translated_text: I shall teach you both the origin and the analysis'—what was said by me, that has been answered by me.

body.translated_text: 'Of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>),

body.text: 19 idam avocad bhagavān āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyananda
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
